I'm [Apurva Nakade](https://apurvanakade.github.io), an Assistant Teaching
Professor in the Applied Mathematics & Statistics department at Johns Hopkins
University. I build these apps for my own classes. Each one takes a single
idea, a numerical method or a visual proof, and makes it something you can
change and watch, rather than something you only read about.

## Using the apps in a class

Every app writes its inputs into its URL, so the address bar is always a link
to exactly what you're looking at. Set up an example, copy the link, and put it
in your notes or a problem set.

You can also put an app straight into another page, such as a course site or
lecture notes. Every app has a **Share** button that writes the embed code for
you; [Embedding an app](embed.qmd) has the details.

## Contributing

The site is open source, on
[GitHub](https://github.com/apurvanakade/VisualMathLab). If something is broken
or confusing, [open an issue](https://github.com/apurvanakade/VisualMathLab/issues).
If you'd like to add an app, the
[contributing guide](https://github.com/apurvanakade/VisualMathLab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
walks through it.
